newsitem.title: USA: Vandals attack black church in rural Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Vandals attack black church in rural Georgia.

text.p: Vandals defaced a 122-year-old black church in rural Georgia, spray-painting hate messages on the door, the cornerstone and across tombstones in an adjacent cemetary, police said on Monday.
Churchgoers discovered the Pleasant Grove Missionary Church daubed by graffiti late on Sunday as they arrived for an evening worship service.

Vandals spray-painted the Ku Klux Klan moniker "KKK" on the front door of the brick sanctuary, along with the name of an inner city street gang whose membership consists mainly of minority youth. The outline of a figure with a gun also appeared on the cornerstone.

"They need help," said the Rev. Melvin Baldwin. "And if there's anything that I can do, I certainly want them to know. I stand with outstretched arms to sit, talk with them, to pray with them, counsel with them as best I know how, to help them through this illness that they must be caught up in."
Police discounted the appearance of the urban street gang's name. "I think that's something they just threw up there," said Sgt. Mike Shinall of the Bartow County Sheriff's Office.
Investigators were looking into the possibility that the vandals came from two nearby mobile home parks, saying suspects in such cases often live close by.
The church stands in a rural area of northwestern Georgia, between Atlanta and Chattanooga, Tennessee, where members of the Ku Klux Klan and other white supremacy groups have been known to be active.
The desecration of a church or cemetary is a felony offence in Georgia.
